An Aniimo can take any job needing its a: An Aniimo can take any job needing its ability at or below its level while it has hours to spare, as long as no two of its facilities want opposite personalities. It has four personalities, one from each pair, shown as letters over its portrait: Instinctive or Energetic (I/E), Nimble or Practical (N/S), Faithful or Tenacious (F/T), Playful or Judicious (P/J). Instalaciones with a resident Aniimo (Sandcastle, Dewy House and the like) need one each, and so does each Horno de calor (Fuego), Unidad de enfriamiento (Hielo) and Lámpara solar (Luz) in use. With My Aniimo, Campo de cultivo and Arboleda jobs only need someone able to do each; they're quick, so they aren't counted against anyone's hours. Not yet checked in game: each recipe's minimum ability level, the Campo de cultivo and Arboleda jobs, and whether an environment building's Aniimo level or personality matters.
Each row is one product; a facility spli: Each row is one product; a facility split between several products gets a row for each. Crops that need a growing environment are grouped by the Horno de calor, Unidad de enfriamiento or Lámpara solar setting that covers them, with its layout. Everything else is grouped like the facility list.
In the Aniimo column, each circle is an: In the Aniimo column, each circle is an ability in its game color with the Aniimo level inside; a ring means the plan counts on the facility's personality bonus. Hover a circle for details.
Every finished batch is carried to the S: Every finished batch is carried to the Storage Unit (SU), so each facility is placed by its trips per hour times its straight-line distance to it: the busiest sit closest, idle ones go to the edge. Each environment building's plots can go anywhere its coverage still reaches them, so they sit on its Storage Unit side. No covered plot reaches another building's coverage, and a crop that needs an environment but is grown without one stays out of all of it, so every crop keeps the temperature the plan gave it. Crops that need no environment can go anywhere. Everything stays within the plots your Nivel de Casa rodante has open (each 20 by 15 tiles; in Advanced mode, the lowest Nivel de Casa rodante that allows what you entered), and the Storage Unit goes wherever the walking comes out least. Hover or tap a facility for its trips and distance. The diagram plays the homeland out in sped-up game time from when everything is set up: each finished batch goes to the Storage Unit (carrying takes no time here), and a recipe starts only once what it takes is there. A ring on each facility shows its batch, amber while it waits for materials. This is a close-packed arrangement worked out step by step, not a proven shortest one.

Every plan is one mixed-integer program: Every plan is one mixed-integer program covering every recipe and facility at once, solved with
. Each recipe your facility levels and m: . Each recipe your facility levels and modules unlock, \(r\), gets a rate \(b_r\) (batches por segundo) and a whole number of units \(u_r\) set to it: plots for a crop, machines for a processed item.
where \\(s_i\\) is how much of item \\(i: where \(s_i\) is how much of item \(i\) is sold por segundo at price \(p_i\), and \(c_r\) is a crop's seed cost. During the Harvest Moon Festival, season crops' seeds cost Moonray Trigo instead, which plans take as unlimited. Subject to:
\\(b_r \\, t_r \\le u_r\\), with \\(u_r\: \(b_r \, t_r \le u_r\), with \(u_r\) a whole number and \(t_r\) the time per batch. A unit runs one recipe and is left running.
Everything made covers what other recipe: Everything made covers what other recipes use plus what's sold. A quick variant makes the same item as the regular one.
For every facility and level \\(L\\), th: For every facility and level \(L\), the units on recipes needing level \(L\) or higher add up to at most what you own at that level. A higher-level plot can run a lower-level recipe.
A crop wanting Cool, Warm, Freeze or Sco: A crop wanting Cool, Warm, Gratisze or Scorching grows at full speed on a plot covered by a Horno de calor or Unidad de enfriamiento set to that mode, and more slowly on an uncovered one (see below). An Adequate crop needs a Lámpara solar and grows nowhere else.
HiGHS proves the plan is the best possib: HiGHS proves the plan is the best possible. On the rare setup where that takes longer than 30 seconds, it stops with the best plan so far and the results say how far from the best it could be. Every plan is then re-checked on its own before it's shown.
Crops and trees take their grow time, le: Crops and trees take their grow time, less the Aniimo's watering: a plot asks for water twice as it grows, at two thirds and at one third of its time left, and each watering takes an eighth of the crop's own time off. A 40-minute crop comes in at 30 and a 4-minute one at 3. A crop short of its environment grows slower but still loses the same minutes, so a Warm crop with no building takes 50 minutes and is watered down to 40; that part isn't checked in game yet.
Everything else has a workload, and how: Everything else has a workload, and how long it takes depends on the Aniimo's Efficiency \(e\), which the facility screen shows, and a base rate \(r\):
At a processor, \\(r\\) is one workload: At a processor, \(r\) is one workload a second. At a gathering facility (Well, Mine, Sandcastle, Dewy House and the like) and at the Dance Pad Polisher and Aniipod Maker, it's higher on recipes needing a higher ability level: 1 a second at level 1, 1.25 at level 2 and 1.5 at level 3. A Growth Fruit, 5,400 workload, takes an hour at 100%.
Efficiency \\(e\\) depends on the Aniimo: Efficiency \(e\) depends on the Aniimo's ability level compared with the level the recipe needs. At exactly the needed level it's 100%. At a processor, one level above the recipe's need is 300%, and each level after that adds 100% (400%, 500%). At a gathering facility, each level above adds half a workload a second, whatever the recipe needs, so against the recipe's own base rate that reads as +50% a level on a level-1 recipe, +40% on a level-2 one and +33% on a level-3 one. The Dance Pad Polisher and Aniipod Maker add 40% a level. The personality term counts only when the Aniimo has the facility's personality (+20%); the Polisher and Aniipod Maker have none. Ability levels stop at 4.
Environments are steps of temperature: F: Environments are steps of temperature: Gratisze -2, Cool -1, no building 0, Warm +1, Scorching +2. A crop grows at 100% at its own, 80% one step away, 50% two steps and 20% beyond that. An uncovered plot is neutral, so a Cool or Warm crop still manages 80% and a Gratisze or Scorching one 50%, which is why plans sometimes grow them with no building at all. Adequate is separate: those crops need a Lámpara solar. Efficiency stretches the grow time, so a Rose at 80% takes 50m instead of 40m for the same 8 roses, before watering.
Temperatures add where two buildings bot: Temperatures add where two buildings both reach a plot, capped at -2 and +2, and the game shows the result on the plot itself: Scorching and Cool together read Warm, Warm and Cool read Room temp. Plans use that, so a Horno de calor on Scorching with four tiles of space to a Unidad de enfriamiento on Cool covers three zones at once, Scorching, Warm between them and Cool. Where the second building sits decides the split: every placement whose coverage still overlaps the first is worked out, in a row or on the diagonal, from touching (6 plots, 24 in the middle and 6, for Campo de cultivo) out to a corner's worth of overlap (22, 10 and 22). Two buildings this close cover fewer plots in total than two standing apart, so a plan only does it when the third zone is worth more. Place the pair exactly as the plan's diagram shows, and keep any other building's area clear of them.
A Cooling Unit is 2×2 tiles, and a Heat: A Unidad de enfriamiento is 2×2 tiles, and a Horno de calor and Lámpara solar one tile each; each covers a 9×9 area centered on it. A plot counts as covered if any part of it is inside, and everything snaps to quarter tiles. Every useful way one building can cover a mix of Campo de cultivo, Arboleda and the rest is worked out once by exact packing; the plan then picks a mode and one of those mixes for each building.
A level-up costs Home Coins \\(C_0\\) pl: A level-up costs Monedas de casa \(C_0\) plus the materials it asks for, \(C_1\) and \(C_2\) (raw Wood Blocks and Mineral Sand up to Casa rodante 6, a Woodworking Bench item and a Chimney Kiln item from Casa rodante 7), and you may already have some of each, \(S_j\). The plan finds the most level-ups per day, \(\lambda\), it could keep up, where for Monedas de casa and each item:
(\\(\\text{made}_j\\) per second), so th: (\(\text{made}_j\) por segundo), so the level-up takes \(1/\lambda\) days. Stock of anything lower in a chain (Wood Blocks, Mineral Sand, a lower tier) counts toward what's made, since the Bench and Kiln process it up. Two more solves follow, each keeping what the last one found: the most Monedas de casa at that pace, then as much extra of the level-up items as spare Bench and Kiln time allows. That's why ore often finishes before wood and shows up as surplus.
Each tier takes 8 of the tier below (4 f: Each tier takes 8 of the tier below (4 for the last), so the Bench and Kiln switch between tiers rather than running one recipe like other processors.
The plan solves once per ticked priority: The plan solves once per ticked priority, in your order. Each solve makes as much of its priority as it can while keeping at least what the earlier ones reached; a last solve then earns as many Monedas de casa as all of those leave room for. Aniimo EXP, Aniipods and, during the Harvest Moon Festival, Harvest Moon Points count as their own currencies, so the same model handles them like Monedas de casa.
Each product starts adding up once its f: Each product starts adding up once its first batch clears its ingredient chain (its lead time), then keeps its steady rate:
This only ever grows with \\(t\\), so th: This only ever grows with \(t\), so the time to reach a target is found by binary search.
If the exact planner can't run (rare; re: If the exact planner can't run (rare; reloading the page usually fixes it), an older planner steps in. It solves the same problem as a continuous linear program, rounds to whole plots and one recipe per machine, then re-solves. Its plans are usually close to the best but not guaranteed, and the results say when it was used.
